THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short) has been filed by the claimants being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 01.02.2022 passed by the MACT, Tiptur in MVC No.809/2014.

2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 28.04.2012 the deceased Mohammed Rehaman Sharif as a driver of the vehicle Tata Innova bearing Registration No.KA-44-M-7779 belongs to respondent No.1 was driving the said vehicle.
Respondent No.1 and his wife Sumaprakash were also traveling in the said vehicle.

That after visiting Tirunelveli, Maduri,
Mahammed Rehaman Sharif, respondent No.1 and his wife Sumaprakash were returning to their native place.

That the said vehicle was driven by driver Mahammed Rehaman NC: 2023:KHC:40532 Sharif very slowly and carefully, at about 01.20 a.m., when the said vehicle was in Netri Nagar fly over, the driver of the lorry bearing Registration No.KA-52-6487, had been parked in the non parking place and no indicator was put on.
Due to said negligent act of the driver of the vehicle bearing Registration No.KA-52-6487, the driver Mahammed Rehaman Sharif dashed his vehicle to the vehicle from back side.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
3. The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased along with interest.
4. On service of summons, the respondent Nos.1, 2 and 5 appeared through counsel and filed written statement in which the averments made in the petition were denied.
It was pleaded that the petition itself is false and frivolous in the eye of law.

The age, occupation and income of the NC:
2023:KHC:40532 deceased are denied.
It was further pleaded that the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant.
Hence, he sought for dismissal of the petition.
5. The respondent Nos.3 and 4 did not appear before the Tribunal inspite of service of notice and hence were placed ex-parte.
6. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.
The claimants, in order to prove their case, examined claimant No.1 as PW-1 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P11.
On behalf of respondents, two witnesses were examined as RW-1 and RW-2 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.R1 to Ex.R3.
The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia

, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, as a result of which, the deceased sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The Tribunal NC: 2023:KHC:40532 further held that the claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.3,23,000/- along with interest at the rate of Smt. Nasim Unnisa vs Mr. Om Prakash on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26213780/
3 9% p.a. and directed respondent No.5 / ICICI Lambord Motor Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.

7. The learned counsel for the claimants has raised the following contentions:
a) Firstly, the claimants claim that the deceased was earning Rs.10,500/- per month by working as driver.
But the Tribunal is not justified in taking the monthly income of the deceased as merely as Rs.6,500/-.

b) Secondly, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -
v- PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS [AIR 2017 SC 5157], in case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 10% of the established income towards 'future prospects' should be the warrant where the deceased was NC: 2023:KHC:40532 aged between the age group of 50-60 years.

sentences.text: The same may be considered.

c) Thirdly, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of PRANAY SETHI (supra), the claimants are entitled for Rs.16,500/- towards 'loss of estate' and Rs.16,500/- towards 'funeral expenses'.
d)

Fourthly, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -V- NANU RAM [2018 ACJ 2782], each of the claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.44,000/- under the head of 'loss of love and affection and consortium'.
e) Fifthly, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of PRANAY SETHI (supra), the compensation awarded under the heads of 'funeral expenses' and 'loss of estate' is on higher side.
f) Lastly, considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

d) Lastly, in view of the Division Bench decision of this Court in the case of MS.JOYEETA BOSE AND OTHERS -V- VENKATESHAN.V AND OTHERS (MFA 5896/2018 AND CONNECTED NC:
2023:KHC:40532 MATTERS DISPOSED OF ON 24.8.2020), the rate of interest granted by the Tribunal at 9% p.a. on the compensation amount is on the higher side.

9. Learned counsel for Oriental Insurance Company has contended that they are only formal party and no liability has been fastened on respondent No.2 i.e. Oriental Insurance Company Limited.

10. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
11.
It is not in dispute that Mohammed Rehaman Sharif died in the road traffic accident occurred on 28.04.2012 due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
12. The claimants claim that deceased was earning Rs.10,500/- per month.
But they have not produced any - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:40532 documents to prove the income of the deceased.
In the absence of proof of income, the notional income has to be assessed.
As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2012, the notional income of the deceased has to be taken at Rs.7,000/- p.m.
To the aforesaid income, 10% has to be added on account of future prospects in view of the law laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in 'PRANAY SETHI' (supra).
Thus, the monthly income comes to Rs.7,700/-.
The Tribunal has rightly deducted 1/3rd of the income of the deceased towards personal expenses.
Thus, the monthly income comes to Rs.5,134/-.
At the time of the accident, the deceased was aged about 56 to 60 years.
Therefore, the multiplier applicable to the age group of 56-60 years is '9'.

Thus, the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.5,54,472/- (Rs.5,134*12*9) on account of 'loss of dependency'.
- 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:40532 13.
In addition, the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.16,500/- on account of 'loss of estate' and compensation of Rs.16,500/- on account of 'funeral expenses'.

14. In view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of 'MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE' (supra), claimant Nos.2, 3 and 4, children of the deceased are entitled for compensation of Rs.44,000/- each under the head of 'loss of parental consortium'.

15. Thus, the claimants are entitled to the following compensation:
 Compensation under Amount in  different Heads (Rs.)
 Loss of dependency 5,54,472  Funeral expenses 16,500  - 12 -  NC: 2023:KHC:40532  Loss of estate 16,500  Loss of spousal 44,000  consortium  Loss of Parental 1,32,000  consortium  Total 7,63,472 16.

In the result, I pass the following order:
ORDER a) The appeal is allowed in part.
b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
c) The claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,63,472/- as against Rs.3,23,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

d) In view of judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of 'MS.JOYEETA BOSE' (supra), the enhanced compensation shall carry interest at 6%
per annum.
